newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary barley,new wheat futures up,old maize down.
newsitem.headline: Hungary barley,new wheat futures up,old maize down.

text.p: Grains futures prices ended mixed on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Monday but traders said only feed barley prices moved on fundamentals.
"Snow and cold weather triggered fears that spring barley planting could be delayed just as it was last year," said Ferenc Kiss of Agrokont.
July feed barley went up 330 forints per tonne to end at 18,820, August rose 300 to 19,150 and October went up by the 400-forint limit to finish at 19,400.
New (1997) crop milling wheat maturities rose 140 to 300 forints but Kiss said one brokerage drove prices up in the last minute after session-long trade below Friday's settlement prices.
"They could have bought earlier any amount at considerably lower prices and the move was clearly aimed at driving up the settlement price," Kiss said.

Old (1996) crop maize prices ended slightly lower, with May closing at 18,100 forints, down 20, and July at 17,600 forints, down 100, but the 144 contracts turnover was small compared with the 9,022 open contracts for the above two months.
Total grains turnover was 257.8 million forints or 604 contracts of which milling wheat accounted for 275.
